Power and energy of the machine's devices

Source: R/hwpwr.R
hwpwr.Rd

Reads what the CPU packages, the memory and the GPUs of this machine draw, from the operating system's own energy counters and power readings, over an interval: dt seconds from now, or since an earlier reading (since). Every figure says how it was obtained, and a device that cannot be measured is listed with the reason, never counted as zero. It is the measured layer under an energy or carbon footprint of a computation.

Usage

hwpwr(
  dt = 1,
  since = NULL,
  step = 0.25,
  rated = NULL,
  pid = Sys.getpid(),
  skip = character(),
  paths = character()
)

Arguments

dt

Seconds to measure over: one number from 0 to 604800 (a week). With 0, one reading (power where a device gives it, for a later since). Not used with since.

since

NULL, or an earlier result of hwpwr() in this session: the interval runs from that reading to now.

step

Seconds between readings within dt: one number above 0.

rated

NULL, or rated powers in watts by kind, c(cpu = , gpu = ): each CPU package's and each GPU's, used for an estimate where a device gives a utilisation but no power.

pid

The process whose share is reported: a process id, a whole number from 0 to 2147483647.

skip

Sources not to use: any of "rapl", "gpu", "battery", "proc", "nvml", "smi", "ioreport", "ioreg", "emi". "gpu" leaves out every graphics processor on Linux and Windows (the kernel's cards and both NVIDIA readers); "nvml" and "smi" leave out one NVIDIA reader each.

paths

Locations to read instead of the system's, by name: root (a folder holding a copy of sys and proc), nvml (the NVIDIA library), smi (the nvidia-smi program), ioreg (the ioreg program); "" turns a program off.

Value

A data frame: kind (cpu, memory, gpu, accelerator, meter, machine or total), vendor, name, scope, watts (the mean over the interval), joules, util (busy share), how, flo, fhi and why. Attributes: dt, the interval in seconds, and snap, the last reading, for since.

Details

Each row is one device (scope = "device"), the share of a device that belongs to the process pid (scope = "process"), the whole machine (scope = "machine", the battery) or the total over the devices (kind = "total"). how is one of

  • "measured counter": the difference of an energy counter;

  • "measured power integrated": power read at every sample, integrated by the trapezoid rule;

  • "rated x utilisation": an estimate, a rated power times the measured utilisation, with the factors flo and fhi between which the true figure may lie (0.4 and 2.9: the power-from-load model of CodeCarbon was off by -60% to +190% against RAPL in its own comparison);

  • "unknown", with the reason in why.

The sources, by system:

  • Linux, CPU and memory: the RAPL counters of the powercap tree (/sys/class/powercap, energy_uj in microjoules). Only the top-level package domains are counted for the CPU and the dram domain for memory; core, uncore and psys are never added (they are parts of a package or more than the CPU). A counter that passes its range (max_energy_range_uj) is unwrapped; a fall that would mean more than half the range, and more than 1 kW could use over the interval, is a reset, and a reading above the range is not a measurement (the row says why). A counter file must be a regular file holding a whole decimal number; anything else is "malformed" or "not a regular file", and is not waited on. A package seen through both the MSR and the MMIO interface is counted once, and per-die copies of one counter (multi-die AMD parts) are counted once. Most distributions let only the administrator read energy_uj; the row then says "not readable: needs read access to the powercap files", and the estimate, when one is made, uses the package's rated power from its constraint_0_max_power_uw.

  • Linux, GPUs: AMD (amdgpu) from the hwmon power1_average or power1_input (microwatts) and gpu_busy_percent; Intel (i915, xe) from the hwmon energy1_input (microjoules) where the kernel has it. Intel's integrated graphics are part of the CPU package figure and are not added again.

  • NVIDIA GPUs (Linux, Windows): the driver's management library (libnvidia-ml.so.1, nvml.dll), loaded at run time: the total energy counter (millijoules), else the power (milliwatts) integrated; the GPU's utilisation and the process's share of its compute samples. Without the library, on Linux, nvidia-smi (power, utilisation, name). A library that is not NVML or does not start, and an nvidia-smi that fails, add no GPU row.

  • macOS on Apple silicon: the energy counters of the IOReport "Energy Model" group (CPU, GPU, neural engine and DRAM), read without administrator rights. IOReport is not a documented public interface of Apple's, so it may change with any release; skip = "ioreport" turns it off. A counter that stops changing before the end of the interval, or whose first step carries energy from before it (a fault reported on newer macOS), is not reported; a pause caught up within the interval is spread over it. The GPU's utilisation comes from ioreg.

  • Windows, CPU and memory: the Energy Meter Interface, the channels named PKG (CPU packages) and DRAM (memory); other channels are listed and not added. Whether a machine has such a meter, and whether an ordinary user may open it, varies; the row says which.

  • The whole machine: the battery's discharge (Linux /sys/class/power_supply, macOS ioreg, Windows the battery's discharge rate), only while it runs on battery. It stands beside the devices and is not added to them.

  • The process's share of a CPU package: the CPU time of pid and its descendants (Linux; on macOS and Windows the calling process with its finished children) over the busy CPU time of the machine, times the package's energy.

Not measurable anywhere here: CPU energy on Linux without read access to the powercap files; most virtual machines and cloud instances (no counters are passed through); memory on CPUs without a DRAM domain; integrated GPUs apart from the CPU package; Intel GPUs on Windows and macOS, and GPUs of other vendors on Windows; CPUs of Intel Macs.

Two readings: a <- hwpwr(0) before a computation and hwpwr(since = a) after it give the energy of the computation. Counters are exact over any interval (but for a counter that could wrap more than once between the readings, which the row notes); a device that gives only power is integrated from the two readings alone. Over dt the devices are read every step seconds. Nothing is written, nothing runs in the background and no network is used.

References

Linux kernel documentation: Power Capping Framework; sysfs ABI of the power supply class; AMDgpu thermal and power interfaces; sysfs ABI of the i915 and xe hwmon interfaces.

NVIDIA. NVML API Reference Guide.

Microsoft. Energy Meter Interface; IOCTL_BATTERY_QUERY_STATUS.

CodeCarbon documentation: Accuracy.

Examples

r <- hwpwr(0.5)
r[, c("kind", "name", "scope", "watts", "joules", "how")]
#>    kind        name  scope watts joules     how
#> 1   cpu         CPU device    NA     NA unknown
#> 2 total all devices device    NA     NA     sum
a <- hwpwr(0)
x <- sum(sqrt(seq_len(1e6)))
b <- hwpwr(since = a)
b[b$kind == "total", c("joules", "why")]
#>   joules              why
#> 2     NA not counted: CPU
